executive_summary:
This dataset records 5,000 purchases at a general retail store across nine departments, with each customer's age and gender, what they bought, how much they paid, the discount applied and how they rated the item.

The data arrived complete, with no missing values. Customer IDs were set aside as identifiers, and text columns with only a handful of values were stored as categories.

Electronics dominates revenue: 895,402 of the 1.43 million total, about 63%, from only one purchase in ten. A typical electronics purchase is around 1,775, more than ten times any other department. Footwear sells the most items (983) but at around 144 each.

Customers are spread evenly between 20 and 70 years old, and age has no meaningful link to how much they spend. Gender and season are almost perfectly balanced, so neither explains differences in sales.

The business depends heavily on electronics. Protecting that department matters most, while growth in footwear and sports, the busiest departments, would reduce that dependence.

executive_summary_zh:
这份数据记录了一家综合零售店九个部门的5,000笔购买，包括顾客的年龄和性别、购买的商品、支付金额、享受的折扣以及对商品的评分。

数据完整，没有缺失值。顾客编号作为标识单独处理，取值较少的文本列以类别形式保存。

电子产品主导了收入：在143万总收入中占895,402，约63%，而购买次数只占十分之一。一笔典型的电子产品购买约1,775，是其他任何部门的十倍以上。鞋类卖出的件数最多（983件），但每件约144。

顾客年龄在20到70岁之间分布均匀，年龄与消费金额没有明显关系。性别和季节几乎完全均衡，都不能解释销售差异。

生意高度依赖电子产品。守住这个部门最重要；而鞋类和运动这两个最繁忙部门的增长，可以降低这种依赖。
